analysis_unit: Recorder-state/action-bounded episode containing retained AOI visits, actions, and projected AX nodes. A bounded adjacent-context window and the linked result state may support cross-state codes, but they do not merge episode boundaries and must be cited explicitly.
visit_caveat: A retained component visit is an AOI-based grouping under project parameters (100 ms minimum, 75 ms sample-gap cap, 150 ms same-component merge gap), not a validated fixation.
population_caveat: Sighted gaze projected onto AX nodes must not be described as blind-user or screen-reader behavior.
coding_rule: Assign at most one primary observed-behavior code, optionally one secondary code, one AX-projection code, one outcome code, and zero or more evidence modifiers. Abstain when minimum evidence is absent.

observed_behavior.name: Directed target acquisition
observed_behavior.definition: A short evidence path reaches a task-relevant unit and is immediately followed by the corresponding action or state transition.
include: Target-relevant unit is visited
The next meaningful action operates on that unit or its direct control
Little or no peer-candidate inspection is present
exclude: Several peer candidates are inspected
A known target is reached through multiple contextual intermediate states; use ORI
The episode only contains an action with no aligned gaze evidence
observed_behavior.minimum_evidence: At least one mapped target-related visit plus a corresponding action or result state.
observed_behavior.confounds: A sparse recording can falsely appear directed.
observed_behavior.positive_example: Visit Search button → click Search → results state.
observed_behavior.borderline_example: One result is clicked after the gaze briefly passes over several unretained candidates.
observed_behavior.ax_signature: No unique signature; often a short local or cross-subtree path.
observed_behavior.screen_reader_implication: Offer an optional context-labeled shortcut while preserving the intermediate structure and original controls.
observed_behavior.confidence: High only when target visit, action, and resulting state align.

observed_behavior.name: Broad candidate scan
observed_behavior.definition: Several peer semantic units are sampled to locate a promising candidate without evidence of pairwise comparison or sustained revisiting.
include: At least four peer candidates or sections are visited
Most candidates receive one retained visit
No repeated A–B–A comparison loop dominates
exclude: Two or more candidates are revisited with attribute evidence; use CMP
The route consists of contextual intermediate states; use ORI
Many visits are caused by one broad noisy container
observed_behavior.minimum_evidence: Ordered visits to at least four non-noisy peer units in one retrieval context.
observed_behavior.confounds: Poor calibration, overlapping boxes, and missing text-level units can create apparent scanning.
observed_behavior.positive_example: Briefly visit five search-result cards, then continue scrolling.
observed_behavior.borderline_example: Four headings in a long article are visited but do not represent interchangeable candidates.
observed_behavior.ax_signature: Often repeated traversal among sibling or nearby subtrees, but no signature is required.
observed_behavior.screen_reader_implication: Provide a concise list overview with role, name, and key metadata; keep the full list reachable.
observed_behavior.confidence: Lower when semantic peer status is uncertain or component granularity is coarse.

observed_behavior.name: Contextual orienteering
observed_behavior.definition: The user reaches a target through small contextual steps where each intermediate state or entity supplies information for the next move.
include: At least two meaningful intermediate states or entities precede the target
Transitions follow contextual links, categories, hubs, or known landmarks
The route is not merely a direct query-result click
exclude: Open-ended query or source reformulation dominates; use EXP
Intermediate states are redirects with no user decision
Only one target-directed action is observed; use DIR
observed_behavior.minimum_evidence: A cross-state route with at least three meaningful nodes and observable contextual transitions.
observed_behavior.confounds: Navigation paths alone do not prove the user consciously used context.
observed_behavior.positive_example: University homepage → department → faculty list → faculty profile.
observed_behavior.borderline_example: Search result → detail → subpage, where the middle page may only be a required gateway.
observed_behavior.ax_signature: Usually includes document resets and movement into new semantic landmarks.
observed_behavior.screen_reader_implication: Preserve breadcrumbs and source-link context; offer state-dependent next-step shortcuts rather than flattening the route.
observed_behavior.confidence: High when intermediate link names and resulting page semantics clearly align.

observed_behavior.name: Iterative exploration or reformulation
observed_behavior.definition: The retrieval strategy, query, source, or working evidence changes across iterations while the user learns or investigates.
include: A query, filter policy, source, or route is observably changed
Multiple iterations contribute different evidence or reject a prior route
The task supports learning, investigation, or cumulative gain
exclude: A fixed known target is reached by contextual stepping; use ORI
A sort control changes only result order and no broader strategy change is visible
Goal evolution is inferred only from dwell
observed_behavior.minimum_evidence: At least two retrieval iterations plus an observable reformulation, source switch, or retained partial evidence.
observed_behavior.confounds: The recording rarely exposes the user's evolving mental information need.
observed_behavior.positive_example: Search query → inspect source → revise query with a discovered term → inspect another source.
observed_behavior.borderline_example: Switch Relevance to New without evidence that the retrieval goal changed.
observed_behavior.ax_signature: Commonly cross-document; no unique within-tree signature.
observed_behavior.screen_reader_implication: Maintain an evidence tray, query history, and source context; do not collapse exploration into one recommended answer.
observed_behavior.confidence: High only with explicit query, source, or policy changes.

observed_behavior.name: Candidate comparison
observed_behavior.definition: Two or more semantically comparable candidates are revisited or inspected through attributes before a choice or continued search.
include: At least two peer candidates exist
At least two candidates are revisited or each is connected to attribute evidence
The sequence provides a basis for a choice, rejection, or unresolved comparison
exclude: Several candidates are viewed once with no return; use SCN
A–B–A crosses unrelated controls
The final choice is known but comparative evidence is absent
observed_behavior.minimum_evidence: Peer-candidate identity plus revisit or candidate-to-attribute transitions for at least two candidates.
observed_behavior.confounds: Component-level boxes may not reveal which attribute text was read.
observed_behavior.positive_example: Candidate A → price A → Candidate B → price B → Candidate A → select A.
observed_behavior.borderline_example: A result card and a filter control alternate repeatedly.
observed_behavior.ax_signature: Often lateral movement among sibling candidate subtrees with returns.
observed_behavior.screen_reader_implication: Create an optional temporary comparison region or table that groups equivalent attributes and preserves links to source candidates.
observed_behavior.confidence: Lower when attribute-level evidence is unavailable.

observed_behavior.name: Return or revisit
observed_behavior.definition: The sequence returns to a previously visited semantic unit, subtree, hub, or document after intervening evidence.
include: A previously visited unit or state is revisited after at least one different meaningful unit
The return is visible in gaze, browser history, or state transition
exclude: Consecutive samples merged into one visit
A duplicate DOM node is mistaken for the same semantic unit
The return is automatically labeled frustration or confusion
observed_behavior.minimum_evidence: A–…–A at the semantic-unit, subtree, or document level.
observed_behavior.confounds: Return may indicate comparison, recovery, confirmation, or ordinary hub navigation; motivation is not encoded by RET.
observed_behavior.positive_example: Detail page → browser Back → result list.
observed_behavior.borderline_example: Gaze returns to the page header after a scroll reset.
observed_behavior.ax_signature: AX return loop or document restoration when snapshots support it.
observed_behavior.screen_reader_implication: Offer recent semantic locations, a context-preserving Back path, or next/previous candidate navigation.
observed_behavior.confidence: High for explicit browser history or stable semantic identity; lower for state-local Cxx identity alone.

observed_behavior.name: Post-action verification
observed_behavior.definition: After an action, the user inspects an observable changed value, selected state, destination, or completion signal.
include: A meaningful action occurs in the source episode
A linked result state or changed region is captured after that action
A subsequent result-state visit targets the changed value, control, destination, or success signal
exclude: Gaze merely returns to the control with no observable state change
A completion label is inferred from task intent alone
The episode ends immediately after the action
observed_behavior.minimum_evidence: Source action + linked observable before/after change + semantically aligned result-state inspection or explicit success signal.
observed_behavior.confounds: Recorder checkpoints may miss the changed state; visual return alone is insufficient.
observed_behavior.positive_example: Select 720p → changed quality state → revisit quality value/player.
observed_behavior.borderline_example: Click a link → inspect the destination title, where this may be ordinary orientation rather than verification.
observed_behavior.ax_signature: Document reset or changed control state followed by a mapped visit.
observed_behavior.screen_reader_implication: Announce the verified change, retain or restore logical focus, and expose the completion signal.
observed_behavior.confidence: High only when the state change is recorded and semantically attributable to the action.

observed_behavior.name: Sparse semantic inspection
observed_behavior.definition: One or more mapped semantic units are inspected, but the available sequence does not support a more specific acquisition, scan, comparison, return, reformulation, orientation, or verification claim.
include: At least one non-noisy semantic-unit visit is available
No more specific observed-behavior code meets its minimum evidence rule
exclude: No mapped semantic-unit evidence is available
A more specific code meets its minimum evidence rule
Only a noisy broad container is mapped
observed_behavior.minimum_evidence: At least one identifiable non-noisy semantic-unit visit; 50–99 ms sensitivity visits are permitted only at low confidence and must be marked as relaxed evidence.
observed_behavior.confounds: Sparse inspection does not establish reading, comprehension, relevance, decision strategy, or target intent.
observed_behavior.positive_example: Visit two content sections once without a return or subsequent aligned action.
observed_behavior.borderline_example: A 65 ms mapped link visit with no other retained evidence; code only as low-confidence relaxed INS.
observed_behavior.ax_signature: No unique signature; preserve the mapped node sequence and evidence tier.
observed_behavior.screen_reader_implication: Do not create a shortcut from INS alone; retain it as descriptive evidence for later cross-episode motifs.
observed_behavior.confidence: Medium for standard retained visits and low when evidence exists only in the 50–99 ms sensitivity pass.

ax_projection.name: Local subtree traversal
ax_projection.definition: Most consecutive projected AX nodes remain within one shallow common ancestor or sibling group.
ax_projection.minimum_evidence: At least two mapped visits with valid ancestry.
ax_projection.interpretation_limit: Describes projected structure, not a screen-reader command.
ax_projection.screen_reader_implication: Consider a region or group-level navigation unit.

ax_projection.name: Cross-subtree traversal
ax_projection.definition: The projected sequence repeatedly moves between structurally separated AX subtrees in the same document.
ax_projection.minimum_evidence: At least two transitions with valid least-common-ancestor evidence.
ax_projection.interpretation_limit: Structural distance does not imply difficulty without an actual screen-reader interaction trace.
ax_projection.screen_reader_implication: A shared virtual region may reduce repeated structural traversal when semantics justify grouping.

ax_projection.name: AX return loop
ax_projection.definition: A projected AX node or semantic subtree is revisited after an intervening mapped node or subtree.
ax_projection.minimum_evidence: A–…–A using stable AX or semantic identity.
ax_projection.interpretation_limit: Does not reveal whether a screen-reader user would use Back, Shift+Tab, heading navigation, or another command.
ax_projection.screen_reader_implication: Expose recent locations or group next/previous navigation.

ax_projection.name: Document or accessibility-tree reset
ax_projection.definition: The recorder document identifier changes and a new AX snapshot becomes current.
ax_projection.minimum_evidence: Before/after document identifiers and AX snapshots.
ax_projection.interpretation_limit: A reset may be navigation, reload, redirect, or tab change.
ax_projection.screen_reader_implication: Announce the new context and establish a predictable initial focus.

ax_projection.name: Insufficient AX projection
ax_projection.definition: Visits lack valid AX nodes, ancestry, state alignment, or sufficient granularity for a structural code.
ax_projection.screen_reader_implication: Do not propose a structural transformation from this episode.

episode_outcome.name: Continued search
episode_outcome.definition: The episode produces a route or evidence state but no selection or verified completion.

episode_outcome.name: Selection or commitment
episode_outcome.definition: A candidate, control, or value is observably selected.

episode_outcome.name: Verified state
episode_outcome.definition: An observable success or changed-state signal is confirmed.

episode_outcome.name: Unresolved
episode_outcome.definition: The episode ends or pivots without task-relevant evidence or a valid next route.

episode_outcome.name: Unknown or insufficient evidence
episode_outcome.definition: The recording does not support an outcome claim.

abstention_rules: No aligned screenshot/DOM/AX state for the relevant action.
Only noisy broad containers are visited.
The code would require inferring intent, comprehension, confusion, frustration, or disability experience.
Candidate or attribute identity cannot be established.
A state change or completion signal required by the code was not recorded.
Two codes remain equally plausible after applying exclusion criteria; mark needs adjudication.
